metric.semantic_determinacy.basis_note: This is a single-language (Java-only) shard. Per spec's common-basis rule, metrics A-D must ultimately be computed on the set of probes for which ALL TEN languages have a fragment; this worker reports Java's per-probe B_i and an all-fragments-basis aggregate (43/44 probes) for the aggregator to reconcile against the common basis once every language's shard is available. The F20.P2 NONE is recorded per NA-2/NA-6 and does not lower this determinacy figure directly; it is captured instead by Capability Coverage.
metric.semantic_determinacy.limitations: B_i values were assigned by expert estimation against the frozen semantic_site_matrix.json rows and capability_universe.json canonical_task text for Java under its frozen recipe (javac, standard library only), not by exhaustive mechanical enumeration of every possible reader misinterpretation; they are recorded here as auditable raw evidence per probe so a reviewer can contest any individual figure without invalidating the aggregate methodology.
metric.semantic_determinacy.method: Per spec 6.1.3.B, for each of the 44 frozen probes we estimated B_i, the count of materially different semantic interpretations (mutation/aliasing/failure/conversion/dispatch/resource/control-flow/representation outcomes) that remain compatible with the probe's local Java surface form (measured_fragment) alone, before consulting external declarations. Raw metric is mean(log2(B_i)) over the probes for which a Java fragment exists (43 of 44; F20.P2 has no fragment because Java's frozen toolchain/recipe provides no mechanism to export a stable unmangled C-ABI symbol, so it is NONE and excluded from this per-language determinacy computation pending the common-basis reconciliation done by the aggregator).
metric.semantic_determinacy.normalization: Since lower branching is better, the 0-100 score is normalized_score = 100 * 2^(-mean_log2_B). This maps B=1 (fully determinate) to 100 and penalizes geometrically as the geometric mean of B_i grows (B=2 -> 50, B=4 -> 25).

rationale_notes.F01.P2: static mutable field vs static final constant: the mutability distinction is explicit via `final`, but a plain (non-volatile) static field leaves a second live interpretation open under the JMM (visibility timing to other threads is unspecified without `volatile`/synchronization), so B=2.
rationale_notes.F05.P1: the bare call site `f(xs)` passes the List reference by value with no local annotation of what `f` will do; from the call-site syntax alone (excluding f's signature per R5) at least 4 materially distinct aliasing/mutation outcomes remain compatible: read-only use, in-place element mutation observable through `xs`, retention of the alias beyond the call, or (if f defensively copies) no observable effect at all.
rationale_notes.F20.P1: Java's Foreign Function & Memory API requires runtime/lookup-object setup whose determinacy of ABI/safety marking is less locally self-evident than in languages with dedicated FFI keywords, so B=2.
